lines.text: The King's Tourney opened on the first frost of winter. Forty thousand people came to watch. A good many of them had come to watch me.
The King's zero, measured twice, and nothing both times. They seated me at the far end of the royal box, between a pillar and a bishop. The bishop moved. Ash took his seat.
Let the King's Tourney begin!
He had to say it twice. The first time, nobody heard him.
In Calvere, Princess, we would say the sun rose twice this morning.
In Aldmere, we'd say you're standing in front of the archery.
The Tourney always opened with the Royal Shoot. The King's own champion, against anyone brave enough to stand beside him.
Sir Lyle, the King's Bow. Gale, five rings. He hadn't lost a shoot in twelve years.
Only one archer stood beside him. A commoner girl from the north, with grey-feathered arrows and her father's bow.
The zero's huntress. Shoot well, girl. They'll remember you were brave.
They'll remember more than that.
Two hundred paces. Both arrows in the heart of the target. Three hundred. The same.
The last mark was a silver ring the size of a coin, hung on a cord at four hundred paces, swinging in the wind.
Sir Lyle called up his Gale. The wind bent around his arrow like a hand. It clipped the ring and set it spinning, and the nobles roared.
Wren called up nothing. Oswin had taught her to hold her rings in, the way Bram did. Today she was a strong three, and nothing more.
She waited. And waited. Until the wind stopped to take a breath.
Her arrow went straight through the ring without touching the silver.
For one heartbeat, there was silence. Then the far end of the field, where the Lowmarket stood, exploded.
That's our Wren! That's the Lowmarket's girl!
Sixty-three threads cheered at once. I felt every one of them. It was the loudest thing I had ever felt.
Not everyone cheered. Down in the champions' enclosure, a man was watching her.
Brother Caddoc. The Order's Hound, who had hunted us on the river road. His rings were bought, and he wore all six of them.
Shoot all the silver you like, girl. The Lists aren't about arrows.
That night, the heralds posted the draw. Wren's first opponent in the Lists was Lord Fane, of the southern march.
He wore a signet ring of milky blue glass.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-six, coming soon.
